## Overview

Prof. Li’s teaching integrates cutting-edge computational data science tools with practical real-world applications. He trains students in modern programming languages and reproducible reporting frameworks, utilizing dynamic simulations to make complex statistical theorems accessible. Additionally, he extends learning beyond the classroom by actively involving undergraduate students in hands-on research projects and the development of open-source statistical software.

## List of Taught Courses

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
library(dplyr)
library(gt)

# Define the two lists of courses with updated local links where applicable
applied_courses <- c(
  "[STAT 244: Elementary Statistical Concepts](https://catalogue.usask.ca/STAT-244)",
  "[STAT 245: Introduction to Statistical Methods](teaching/stat245/)",
  "[STAT 345: Design and Analysis of Experiments](teaching/stat345/)",
  "[STAT 348: Sampling Techniques](teaching/stat348/)",
  "[STAT 834: Advanced Experimental Design](teaching/stat345/)",
  "[STAT 845: Statistical Methods for Research](teaching/stat845/)",
  "[STAT 848: Multivariate Data Analysis](https://catalogue.usask.ca/STAT-848)"
)

theory_courses <- c(
  "[STAT 241: Probability Theory](https://catalogue.usask.ca/STAT-241)",
  "[STAT 242: Statistical Theory and Methodology](https://catalogue.usask.ca/STAT-242)",
  "[STAT 342: Probability and Mathematical Statistics](teaching/stat342/)",
  "[STAT 442/850: Statistical Inference](teaching/stat850/)",
  "[STAT 443/851: Linear Statistical Models](teaching/stat851/)",
  "[STAT 420/812: Computational Statistics](teaching/stat812/)",
  "[STAT 841: Probability Theory](https://catalogue.usask.ca/202003/STAT-841)"
)

# Automatically pad the shorter column with empty strings so they match in length
max_len <- max(length(applied_courses), length(theory_courses))
length(applied_courses) <- max_len
length(theory_courses) <- max_len

applied_courses[is.na(applied_courses)] <- ""
theory_courses[is.na(theory_courses)] <- ""

# Create the data frame
courses <- data.frame(
  Applied_Stat = applied_courses,
  Stat_Theory_Algorithms = theory_courses
)

# Generate the gt table
courses %>%
  gt() %>%
  cols_label(
    Applied_Stat = "Applied Statistics",
    Stat_Theory_Algorithms = "Statistical Theory and Algorithms"
  ) %>%
  fmt_markdown(columns = everything()) %>%
  cols_align(align = "left") %>%
  tab_options(
    table.width = pct(100),
    column_labels.font.weight = "bold"
  )
```
